headline: Claude's AI is eating the jobs of its own humans. What does that signal for the rest of us?
deck: Anthropic's own study shows juniors fell from 27% to 9% of its new technical hires as AI took on the first draft. If nobody hires juniors, who trains the seniors you'll need in 2030?
video_title: Claude's AI is eating the jobs of its own humans. What does that signal for the rest of us?
comment_question: WHO WILL BE YOUR SENIORS IN 2030?
endnote: Figures checked on 31 October 2026 against the sources below.

figures.after: and the job held up or came back bigger.
figures.alt: Twice the job came back bigger: city bank branches needed 13 tellers instead of 20 but opened 43% more branches, and spreadsheets cut 400,000 clerk jobs while adding 600,000 accounting jobs. At Anthropic, juniors fell from 27% to 9% of new technical hires.

Six hours of agent work for every hour of staff: by August, the hours Anthropic's AI agents worked outnumbered its employees' hours six to one. Juniors' share of its technical teams fell from 21% to 14% since early 2025, and about one in three of its machine learning managers said they were hiring less because of AI.

figures.after: If nobody hires them, nobody trains them.
figures.alt: The seniors of 2030 are juniors today. A junior learns the job by doing the dull, repeating work; the middle years of getting it wrong and being put right are the work AI now does first; a senior in 2030 needs the judgement, with nowhere left to grow it. Anthropic's own staff expect AI to be able to do 75% of their work by 2030.
